name: NB International Pro
classification_notes: A broad-coverage grotesque built as a general-purpose corporate system, spanning Latin, Cyrillic and Greek in its CG Edition.
summary: A broad grotesque system extended to Cyrillic and Greek, built for corporate identity work across scripts.
description: NB International Pro is Neubau's most script-extensive family, running to five roman weights plus a monospace cut, all with italics and coverage across Latin, Cyrillic and Greek in its CG Edition. It reads as a general-purpose corporate grotesque rather than a distinctive display face. Useful where multi-script consistency matters more than character.
foundry_blurb: Neubau positions NB International Pro CG Edition as an 11-typeset system supporting Latin, Cyrillic and Greek scripts across 110+ languages.

name: NB Form
classification_notes: Part of Neubau's constructed grotesque system, built on the studio's grid-based approach to letterform construction.
summary: A constructed grotesque from Neubau's in-house system, sold as a single Std edition.
description: NB Form follows Neubau's usual approach of building letterforms from a strict internal grid rather than optical correction. Sold as a single Std edition without an expanded weight range or italic. More a supporting player in the Neubau catalogue than a flagship family.
foundry_blurb: Neubau lists NB Form Std as part of its constructed typeface system, following the studio's grid-based design method.

name: NB Akademie
classification_notes: A large, systematic grotesque family with matching monospace and italic cuts across every weight, built as a full corporate type system.
summary: A 32-style grotesque system running eight weights with matching italics and monospace cuts.
description: NB Akademie is Neubau's largest single system: eight weights from Light to Black, each with an italic and a monospace counterpart, sold as Std and Pro editions with different language coverage. It's built for organisations that need one consistent voice across every context rather than a typeface with strong character. Comprehensive rather than distinctive.
foundry_blurb: Neubau describes NB Akademie as a contemporary sans serif type system comprising 32 styles, available as OpenType Std and Pro editions.

name: NB Typewriter Pro
designer: Stefan Gandl, with Akane Sakai and Moritz Otten
classification_notes: Built directly on NB Grotesk's construction but in fixed-width form, this reads as a typewriter-style monospace.
summary: A typewriter-style monospace built on NB Grotesk's grid, with an alternate rounded-serif cut.
description: NB Typewriter Pro carries over NB Grotesk's constructed logic into a fixed-width, typewriter-flavoured face. Three weights come in both a standard cut and an alternate with rounded serifs. A functional companion piece rather than a standalone design statement.
foundry_blurb: Neubau describes NB Typewriter Pro as based on the construction of NB Grotesk, additionally available in an alternate style with rounded serifs.

name: NB Fett
classification_notes: The name translates from German as 'bold' or 'fat', and the face is built as a single heavyweight display grotesque.
summary: A single heavyweight grotesque, one of Neubau's earliest releases, sold as a standalone Std edition.
description: NB Fett is a single-weight, deliberately heavy grotesque dating back to 2002, reissued as a Std edition. It's built for impact at display sizes rather than range. One of the plainer entries in Neubau's catalogue.
foundry_blurb: Neubau lists NB Fett Std as part of its typeface catalogue, credited to Stefan Gandl with a 2016 Std edition of the original 2002 design.

name: NB Architekt
classification_notes: A classic monoline monospace built to reference architectural lettering, so it's classified as mono rather than sans-serif.
summary: A classic monoline monospace paying tribute to lettering on architectural construction plans.
description: NB Architekt references the lettering used on architectural plans during the Letraset era, built as a strict monoline monospace across three weights. A rounded variant followed in 2005 and a lighter cut in 2007. Technical and specific rather than an everyday text face.
foundry_blurb: Neubau describes NB Architekt as paying tribute to typefaces used on architectural construction plans during the 'Letraset' era, a classic modern monoline monospace originally designed for Neubau studio.

name: NB Plan Pro
classification_notes: A general grotesque sold as a single Pro edition without an expanded weight range, part of Neubau's constructed type system.
summary: A single-weight grotesque with wide Latin language coverage, sold as a Pro edition.
description: NB Plan Pro is a plain, functional grotesque with 433 characters and broad Latin-extended coverage. No additional weights or italics are offered. A supporting face rather than a flagship release.
foundry_blurb: Neubau lists NB Plan Pro with 102+ Latin-based language support and a 433-character set, available in OTF, TTF and webfont formats.

name: NB Television Pro
classification_notes: The 2D, 3D and mono variants push this beyond a standard sans into experimental display territory built for screen and motion contexts.
summary: An experimental display system with 2D, 3D and monospace cuts built for screen and motion work.
description: NB Television Pro is one of Neubau's more experimental releases, offering six typesets including extruded 2D and 3D styles alongside a standard and monospace cut. It's built more for motion graphics and screen contexts than running text. Distinctive rather than neutral.
foundry_blurb: Neubau describes the complete NB Television Pro set as including six typesets: Regular, 2D, 3D, Mono, Mono 2D and Mono 3D.

name: NB Grotesk
classification_notes: A monoline neo-grotesque built on a strict diamond grid with no optical correction, giving it a deliberately raw grotesque character.
summary: Neubau's most recognisable typeface, a monoline neo-grotesque built without optical correction on a strict diamond grid.
description: NB Grotesk was developed for the 'Neubauism' exhibition in Eindhoven in 2008 and remains the studio's most widely used family. Six weights follow a diamond-grid construction that deliberately skips optical correction, giving it a raw, slightly mechanical character. Rounded and monospace siblings extend it further.
foundry_blurb: Neubau describes NB Grotesk as a constructed monoline neo grotesk typeface based on Gandl's diamond grid system, whose no-optical-corrections rule gives it raw, typical characteristics as Neubau's most popular typeface.

name: NB Grotesk Pro Mono
classification_notes: The fixed-width version of NB Grotesk, including a stencil cut, so it's classified as mono rather than sans-serif.
summary: The monospace cut of NB Grotesk, with an added stencil style for extra display use.
description: NB Grotesk Pro Mono carries the parent family's diamond-grid construction into a fixed-width form across four styles, including a stencil variant. Suits code and technical layouts that still want Neubau's raw, constructed character. A direct extension rather than a separate design.
foundry_blurb: Neubau describes NB Grotesk as originally developed for the 'Neubauism' exhibition in Eindhoven in 2008, and remains Neubau's most popular typeface today, here extended into a Pro Mono edition.

name: NB Grotesk-R
classification_notes: The rounded cut of NB Grotesk, softening the same diamond-grid construction with rounded terminals.
summary: The rounded companion to NB Grotesk, keeping its constructed diamond-grid logic with softer terminals.
description: NB Grotesk-R applies the same strict diamond-grid construction as its parent but rounds off the terminals for a friendlier reading. Six weights match the standard cut. A variant rather than a distinct release.
foundry_blurb: Neubau describes NB Grotesk-R as sharing NB Grotesk's constructed monoline neo grotesk system, based on Gandl's diamond grid, in a rounded edition.

name: NB Rietveld
classification_notes: Built on a rigid 9x9 grid referencing furniture construction, this is a strict geometric sans with a strong conceptual basis.
summary: A rigidly gridded geometric sans inspired by the construction elements of Rietveld's 'Red and Blue' chair.
description: NB Rietveld builds every letterform from a strict 9x9 grid, taking its cue from the simplicity of Gerrit Rietveld's furniture design. Single weight, no italic, and currently listed as sold out on the foundry's own shop. More a design object than a working text face.
foundry_blurb: Neubau describes NB Rietveld as inspired by a copy of Rietveld's 'Red and Blue' chair owned by Wim Crouwel, interpreting the overall look and simplicity of the chair's construction elements using a rigid 9 by 9 grid.
